data.gender_notes: Khaadhi is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'h-d-h', meaning to judge, decide, or arbitrate. In Islamic history, the title 'Khaadhi' was given to respected scholars and judges who upheld justice and Islamic law. This name symbolizes wisdom, fairness, and the pursuit of knowledge. The name Khaadhi carries the meaning “Judge, Arbiter, Decider” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Khaadhi usually hope their child will grow to embody judge, arbiter, decider and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Hence, the title 'Khaadhi' embodied the values of justice, knowledge, and wisdom within Islamic culture, inspiring awe and respect.
